source: Zhang et al. (2024), results of RQ1.xlsx
snippet: whole function simulate_quicksort, lines 146 to 182 of the original, with the nested functions partition (148 to 164) and quicksort (166 to 176)
nested_functions: partition (line 148, PAR=7) and quicksort (line 166, PAR=7) are inside simulate_quicksort (line 146, PAR=5). By the outermost-function rule, the three detections form a single instance. Removing the smell applies to all three.
external_dependencies: none: the snippet does not touch pygame; the helper functions do, and they became pure-Python scaffolding
copied_verbatim: lines 68 to 73: body of compare_elements (the signature changed, see scaffolding)
lines 77 to 89: body of compare_and_swap (the signature changed, see scaffolding)
comments_in_snippet: Kept, by rule 1 (verbatim snippet), the comment '# generated by github copilot' on line 147, which reveals the origin of the code, and the commented-out line '# pivot = arr[high]' (150). Same treatment as the docstring of LPL-01: recorded as a limitation.
removed_from_original: lines 1 to 3, imports of sys, pygame, os and random: not used by the snippet or the scaffolding.
lines 5 to 8 and 10 to 16, colors, window size, PROP and comments: they only served the real drawing; clock = None (line 10) became the clock of the scaffolding.

draw_element (19), get_element_texts (35), matrix_comparisons (52), simulate_bubblesort (92), simulate_insertionsort (102), simulate_heapsort (113), simulate_sort_algorithm (185) and the __main__ block (213): outside the snippet and not called by it.
scaffolding: draw_array: same signature as the original (4 parameters counted; the default of poses_elevated became an empty tuple instead of a list); instead of drawing with pygame, it stores a frame on the screen: (texts in the current order, highlighted positions, width, height).

compare_elements and compare_and_swap: bodies copied from the original (lines 68 to 73 and 77 to 89), signatures changed from (display, arrTexts, width_reference, height_reference, arr, i, j) to (display, arrTexts, *args), unpacking the rest in the first line. With 7 parameters they would trigger LPL in the scaffolding (PAR=7), and removing the smell would be impossible; the calls in the snippet, with 7 positional arguments, still work.
_Text (already rendered text, only the value), _Screen (list of frames) and _Clock (stores the rate of each tick); clock is a module-level _Clock, like the global of the original.
run(values): sorts a copy, with width 40 and height 100, and returns (sorted list, frames, tick rates).
Checked: Pysmell only flags simulate_quicksort (PAR=5), partition (PAR=7) and quicksort (PAR=7); nothing in the scaffolding.
pinned_behavior: typical: [1, 3, 0, 2] becomes [0, 1, 2, 3]; the 21 frames in the exact order (4 comparisons and 3 swaps, going through the branch where i == j and there is no swap, the branch where the element goes past the pivot and the recursion on the left side), width and height passed on without swapping, and 21 ticks at rate 3. Step-by-step count in the docstring of the test.
edge: empty list; only the final frame and 1 tick.
invalid: [3, 'a', 1] raises TypeError in the comparison.
not_pinned_on_purpose: Identity of the sorted list: run sorts a copy and returns the result; the test checks the content.
Real drawing (colors, positions in pixels): the scaffolding does not draw, it only records what would be drawn.
